body.objective: Students will be able to use advanced techniques.
successCriteria: I can apply advanced techniques in my CTS area
I can follow an industry workflow
I can mentor a newer student in a skill
body.hook: At the advanced level, you're not just learning techniques; you're expected to work like an industry professional. That means following real workflows, working efficiently and passing on your skills to others, the way a journeyperson trains an apprentice.

vocabulary.definition: The organized sequence of steps used to complete a job.
A level of quality or method accepted in a profession.
Getting a quality result with the least wasted time and material.
An experienced person who guides someone less experienced.
A certified tradesperson who has completed an apprenticeship.
Focusing on one area of a field in depth.

study.title: Work Like a Pro
study.question: How do professionals work, and how do they pass on their skills?
study.passage:
Part 1, Industry workflow (10 minutes): Research the workflow for one professional task in your area:
• Commercial kitchen: mise en place → cook to order → plate → quality check → clean as you go.
• Carpentry: measure twice → mark → cut → test fit → assemble → finish.
• Software development: plan → write code → test → review → deploy → fix.
• Graphic design: brief → research → sketches → digital drafts → client feedback → final files.
Part 2, Advanced task (25 minutes): Complete an advanced task following the workflow, timing each step. Examples: plate a three-component dish to a standard; build a box with a dado or rabbet joint; write a program with functions and error handling; design a brand logo set with colour and type specifications.
Part 3, Efficiency review (5 minutes): Which step took longest? Where did you waste time or material?
Part 4, Mentoring (15 minutes): Teach a CTS 10 student (or a classmate) one skill using: explain → demonstrate → guided practice → independent practice → feedback.
Industry connection: in Alberta's apprenticeship system, journeypersons train apprentices on the job. The Registered Apprenticeship Program (RAP) lets high school students start that training while earning credits.
study.source: Original activity written for this lesson; apprenticeship information from Alberta Apprenticeship and Industry Training and alis.alberta.ca.
